description: Stone fruit grown in the mid-hills of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir, with low-chill varieties in the Punjab and western Uttar Pradesh plains. It needs winter chilling and is rarely grown in South India.
npk_split: For full-bearing trees: apply FYM with all P and K in December-January, half the N before flowering and the rest after fruit set.

Bacterial spot.name: Bacterial Spot
Bacterial spot.description: Bacterial disease of leaves, twigs and fruits that is worst in warm, windy, rainy weather. It causes shot-holed leaves, early leaf fall and pitted, cracked fruits.
symptoms: Small angular water-soaked spots, often clustered near the leaf tip and midrib
Spots turn purple-brown and the centres fall out, leaving shot holes
Spotted leaves turn yellow and drop early
Small sunken dark spots and cracks on fruit skin
Dark sunken cankers on young twigs
Bacterial spot.spread: Wind-driven rain carries bacteria from twig cankers to young leaves and fruits, entering through leaf pores and wounds.
Bacterial spot.action: Spray a copper fungicide at leaf fall and again before bud swell, and prune out twigs with cankers.

treatment.name: Copper oxychloride 50 WP
treatment.notes: At leaf fall and at bud swell only; copper scorches peach leaves when sprayed in full leaf.

treatment.name: Open-canopy pruning and moderate nitrogen
treatment.notes: Leaves dry faster in an open tree; excess nitrogen makes soft growth that is easily infected.

treatment.name: Tolerant varieties and disease-free nursery plants
treatment.notes: Use for new plantings in areas where the disease is regular.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.description: The leaf shows no sign of disease, pest or deficiency. Keep following the regular orchard care schedule.
symptoms: Uniform green leaves without spots or holes
No curling, blistering or early leaf fall
healthy.spread: Not applicable - no disease or pest detected.
healthy.action: Continue regular pruning, balanced manuring and weekly scouting of the orchard.
